svg.title: Figure 4. When the deformation changes the eccentricity
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) A bar between two rigid end blocks that are pinned on the load line, a distance a beyond each end of the free length L; the bar's centerline starts a distance e from the load line. Under tension the bar bends toward the load line and the eccentricity at mid-length shrinks; under compression the bar bows away from the load line and the eccentricity grows. (b) The bending moment divided by P times e, plotted against the axial load as a fraction of the buckling load of the member with its end blocks. At mid-length the curves for end blocks of zero length and of one tenth of the free length nearly coincide: the factor is 1 at zero load, falls below 1 in tension and rises without bound as the compressive load approaches buckling. At the ends of the free length the factor changes much less. A narrow band around 1 marks where the superposition formula, which assumes the factor is 1, is within 5 percent.
